characteristics.title: LLHR: Low Latency and High Reliability CNN Distributed Inference for Resource-Constrained UAV Swarms
characteristics.venue: 2023 IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference (WCNC)
characteristics.uav_architecture_role_and_topology: UAV cameras generate image classification requests; same-altitude UAVs cooperate over a wireless ad hoc network. The inference path is intra-swarm.
characteristics.inference_model_task_and_dataset: Surveillance image classification using LeNet and AlexNet. The evaluated image dataset is not named in §IV.
characteristics.partition_and_assignment: Discrete assignment of each CNN layer to one UAV, with memory and compute bounds and modeled delegation on insufficient capacity.
characteristics.evaluation_platform_simulator_hardware_a: Simulation with synthetic surveillance grid and Raspberry Pi B+ device profiles. Figures 2–5 show average latency and minimum radio transmit power; Fig. 5 uses static-path and random-movement baselines.
characteristics.mobility_channel_intermittency_failure_a: The link model is line-of-sight and distance dependent; position choice respects modeled separation. The minimum transmission-rate constraint represents link reliability. No outage, link loss or failure/recovery trial is reported in §IV.

appraisal.rationale: The distributed inference question, placement and peer communication system are stated; §III specifies the objectives.
appraisal.quote: form a wireless ad hoc network

appraisal.rationale: Same altitude, LoS and constrained compute, memory and power are described. Interference and non-line-of-sight are not modeled (see §V future work).
Device, grid and link assumptions are reported. Solver configuration, repeat or seed details and a complete comparator configuration are not given in §III–IV.

appraisal.rationale: Static-path and random movement baselines are described. Fig. 5 text does not fully specify CNN, radio or device configuration.
appraisal.quote: the UAVs have a static path to follow

appraisal.rationale: Average latency and minimum radio transmit power match their objectives. Reliability is modeled as a rate constraint; §IV presents no measured outage or delivery outcome.
appraisal.quote: Average Latency for Different Requests in Different Models

appraisal.rationale: The figures sweep request load, radio settings and swarm size across conditions. No repeated-run variability is reported in §IV.
appraisal.quote: as we vary the number of

appraisal.rationale: Distance-dependent channel and grid position constrain the simulation. The link model omits NLoS and interference effects, and §IV reports no mobility interruption trial.
The conclusion identifies simulations and deferred channel tests, but interprets the model constraint broadly as guaranteed transmission reliability.
